why_the_pair_is_not_independent: Both legs depend on the same passing volume and on the same quarterback's availability and efficiency
what_must_be_measured: Joint rate of both legs versus the product of the two marginals, on paired settled legs
estimator: Joint rate minus product of marginals with a bootstrap interval
required_sample: Paired settled legs with the provider's exact thresholds

why_the_pair_is_not_independent: Scoring and passing volume share the same drives, so a shootout raises both
what_must_be_measured: Joint rate of both legs versus the product of the two marginals
estimator: Joint rate minus product of marginals with a bootstrap interval

why_the_pair_is_not_independent: A back who is used heavily between the tackles may be used less as a receiver when the team leads
what_must_be_measured: Joint rate of both legs versus the product of the two marginals
estimator: Joint rate minus product of marginals with a bootstrap interval

why_the_pair_is_not_independent: A cover and a team total can be satisfied or broken by the same scoring play, so the legs are not free to vary independently
what_must_be_measured: Joint rate of both legs versus the product of the marginals, after verifying the provider's settlement definition
estimator: Joint rate compared with the product of marginals under the provider's rule text
required_sample: Paired settled legs and the rule text

leg_b: Both teams to score over threshold
why_the_pair_is_not_independent: If both teams score, the game total has at least a floor, so the legs are algebraically linked
what_must_be_measured: Derive the logical implication first, then measure the joint rate on settled legs
estimator: Implication table plus the measured joint rate

leg_a: Two legs in the same game
why_the_pair_is_not_independent: Weather, rest and referee assignment can co-move across games on the same day even when the games are separate
what_must_be_measured: Cross-game joint rate versus the product of the marginals, with week-clustered uncertainty

why_the_pair_is_not_independent: The market may already price the same availability news, so the two are not separate evidence
what_must_be_measured: Correlation between the signal value and the price change, using only point-in-time observations
estimator: Paired correlation with a bootstrap interval

why_the_pair_is_not_independent: Two signals built from the same unit-exposure input can pick the same games
what_must_be_measured: Correlation of the paired out-of-sample forecast or paper-return series on the same event set
estimator: Paired series correlation with week-clustered uncertainty

leg_b: Starter absence in week N plus 1
why_the_pair_is_not_independent: A long-term injury causes correlated absences in consecutive weeks, which can double-count the same cause
what_must_be_measured: Autocorrelation of the unit-exposure series with a stated lag
estimator: Lag correlation on verified weekly snapshots

leg_a: Player prop with a replacement starter
leg_b: The same player's prop in the previous game
why_the_pair_is_not_independent: A role change makes the previous game's opportunity distribution the wrong reference
what_must_be_measured: Difference in the opportunity distribution before and after the role change, with an interval
required_sample: Official gamebook role data for consecutive weeks
